coordinates.origin: Lowest preserved bone contact centre; support separate if needed

concept.reason: Direct museum fossil plate + primary anatomical description sufficient for preserved ramus study; extra synthetic concepts would not add factual evidence.

specimen_reference: NHM P3317, left mandibular ramus, Woodward catalogue Plate XII Fig1
scope: Preserved single deep, narrow left lower-jaw ramus study. No full fish, upper skull, opposite mirrored ramus or soft tissue. Retain broken/missing zones rather than inventing a pristine complete jaw.
geology: Lower Carboniferous Limestone, Gilmerton, Scotland, for P3317 plate record.
material_policy: Original palette-only opaque PBR fossil bone with muted brown/grey and subtly darker tooth surfaces; no image texture or copyrighted source embedding. Small vermicular surface relief optional; do not turn sculpt into noisy grooves.

scale.method: Plate XII Fig1 is printed one-third natural size. Its approximately 950 px horizontal span in rendered page686 at 2200px height / page height562.6pt yields approximately 0.257m after 3x scaling. Check against Fig3 clavicle on companion plate, stated 0.32m in text, suggests similar order. Round to 0.27m and disclose scan/plate uncertainty approximately 10–15%; thickness is a separate artistic estimate from narrow-jaw description.
scale.prohibition: Do not label 0.27m an exact museum measurement; do not substitute dimensions from the St Andrews slab or isolated 0.17m tusk from different specimens.

diagnostic_targets: Deep elongate ramus, much narrower across the jaw than tall; long low tooth-bearing dorsal border over a substantial ventral infradentary wall.
Plate XII Fig1: one prominent mesial/anterior tusk, two distinct large mid-ramus fangs and smaller irregular teeth; maintain visual hierarchy instead of equal-size pickets.
Modern primary description distinguishes dentary marginal row from lingual coronoid fangs. Offset fangs toward lingual edge; do not put all teeth on a single centreline.

Maintain single fossil ramus and preserved outlines. No invented opposite-side pair or upper jaw; original paired large-fang cue is conveyed by the two evident coronoid fangs on the preserved segment.
Raised distal/posterior process, subtle outer bone divisions and narrow open inner jaw region. No complete solid box-girder or ossified Meckelian fill.
Conical, gently recurved teeth; not mammalian molars, serrated tyrannosaur blades or modern shark triangles.
uncertainties: P3317 external plate supplies preserved silhouette, not all internal surfaces. Modern Rhizodus text supports internal structural interpretation, not exact P3317 measured interior.
Thickness and internal relief are restrained artistic interpretation and must be disclosed. No exact replica/scan claims.
Modern primary full text read; its photographic PDF/image endpoints returned403, so those images were NOT inspected. Historic Plate XII Fig1 was inspected directly and is the frozen visual authority.
Do not add missing third coronoid fang solely because complete species jaw has three coronoids; preserve plate-supported segment.
acceptance_checklist: Side silhouette matches long deep single ramus and prominent tooth-size hierarchy in Plate XII Fig1.
Top view clearly shows narrow jaw and offset marginal/coronoid tooth positions.
No upper jaw, whole fish, mirrored counterpart or unsupported restored missing bones.
Meter scale is declared approximate plate-derived, not exact specimen size.
Four exact-GLB views, rebuild twice and standard tests; independent review records uncertainties.
